Thursday July 9, 2026 evening. The July 9 evening brief holds at Vibe 4 — restoring the July 8 evening level after the July 8 morning's Vibe 3 downgrade driven by the overnight tanker-strike/CENTCOM-retaliation/Iran-counter-strike escalation sequence. The session's analytical signature is a genuine tension between the PNW fire picture's substantial improvement and the Hormuz re-escalation's continued ambiguity. On fires: Chelan Hills Fire achieving 50% containment on Day 5 (from 20% on Day 4, from 0% on Day 3) is the most significant domestic infrastructure positive of the week — 200+ personnel built line geometry on east-of-Cascades terrain that has progressed from zero to majority containment in 48 hours. Navarre Coulee's de-escalation to Level 1 and 80% containment removes it from active threat status. The SR-20 and Skagit dam power situation is the session's primary infrastructure uncertainty, with the Day 5 Sourdough ICS-209 the critical pending indicator. On Hormuz: Trump declared the ceasefire/MOU 'over' at the NATO summit in Ankara on July 8, but the statement was accompanied by a critical qualifier: 'I think the agreement is over. But Steve [Witkoff] and Jared [Kushner], they want to keep going — but they have to come back to me.' That qualifier — acknowledging ongoing negotiator willingness while reserving personal authority — is the MOU's survival thread. No formal termination instrument was issued. No blockade reinstatement order was confirmed. CENTCOM conducted additional strikes (second wave on July 8 evening targeting Sirik, Qeshm, Bandar Abbas, Iranshahr, Bushehr, Konarak, Chabahar) but characterized them as degradation operations rather than war-resumption operations. Iran struck 85+ US facilities in Bahrain and Kuwait — the largest single Iranian counter-strike of the post-MOU period — but did not formally void the MOU or declare Hormuz re-closed at the SNSC level (re-closure remains operative but under the pre-existing June 26 IRGC cargo-strike rationale, not a new MOU-void declaration). Kharg Island — through which 90% of Iran's oil exports transit — was threatened but not struck. The WTI price at ~$75 on July 9 (above the $74 normalization floor) is a war-premium price, not a normalization-confidence price: the commodity market is pricing re-escalation risk, not deal stability.

vibe.rationale: Vibe 4 — holds at the July 8 evening level, restoring from the July 8 morning Vibe 3 downgrade. The July 9 evening session represents the most analytically balanced point of the post-MOU arc: genuine positive infrastructure developments offsetting genuine geopolitical deterioration at near-equal weight. Fire improvement positive: Chelan Hills achieving 50% containment is categorically the most significant domestic infrastructure improvement since the July 4 ignition cluster began. At Day 3 (July 6 morning), Chelan Hills was at 0% containment with 100+ structures destroyed — a generational destruction event by the Douglas County Fire Marshal's 30-year benchmark. At Day 5 (July 9 evening), 50% containment with the same ~9,735-acre ICS footprint means line geometry is established, structural loss rate is stabilized, and personnel are shifting from initial attack to extended containment mode. Navarre Coulee at 80% contained/Level 1 is functionally resolved. The SR-20 and Skagit dam situation is the remaining active uncertainty. Hormuz deterioration negative: Trump's 'ceasefire over' statement at the NATO Ankara summit (July 8) is the most extreme US presidential MOU-status language since the June 19 signing. The CENTCOM second-wave strikes (July 8 evening) targeting six Iranian locations and Iran's counter-strike against 85+ US military facilities in Bahrain and Kuwait constitute the most geographically extensive military exchange of the entire post-MOU period. Oil sanctions on Iranian crude were reimposed July 7 — stripping the MOU's central economic incentive for Iranian participation. Kharg Island was threatened. Against these: Witkoff and Kushner publicly want to continue negotiations ('but they have to come back to me' — Trump); no formal MOU termination instrument; no SNSC formal MOU-void declaration; CENTCOM framing operations as 'degradation' not 'war resumption'; Iran has not issued a new MOU-void declaration (re-closure remains under prior June 26 rationale). The balance: on Hormuz, the formal structures of the MOU persist under maximum stress without a decisive breach instrument; on fires, the PNW's worst active fire event of the season has turned from crisis to managed containment in 48 hours. Upgrade to Vibe 5 requires: Iran/Witkoff announcement of formal negotiation resumption framework or ceasefire restoration; Sourdough Day 5 ICS-209 showing any containment; WTI declining from ~$75 re-escalation premium toward $69-71 range (de-escalation signal). Drop to Vibe 3 requires: Iran SNSC formally voiding MOU in response to oil-sanction reimposition; CENTCOM reinstating Project Freedom naval blockade under Kharg Island seizure operation; Chelan Hills regression below 50% under post-AR wind event; Sourdough zero containment through Day 5 with fire-perimeter threat to Skagit dam complex.

items.summary: The July 9 evening Hormuz session is defined by the gap between Trump's declaratory posture and the MOU's formal operational status. On declaration: Trump stated 'as far as I'm concerned, it's over' at the NATO summit close-out press conference in Ankara, Turkey on July 8 — the most extreme MOU-status presidential language since the June 19 signing. He threatened to 'hit Iran VERY HARD TONIGHT' and said the US might 'take over Kharg Island' — through which approximately 90% of Iran's oil exports transit. On operations: CENTCOM executed a second wave of strikes on July 8 targeting Sirik, Qeshm, Bandar Abbas, Iranshahr, Bushehr, Konarak, and Chabahar in southeastern Iran plus Aq Qala in northeastern Iran — the most geographically dispersed CENTCOM strike package since the initial Project Freedom operations. Iran responded with strikes on 85+ US military facilities across Bahrain and Kuwait — the largest single Iranian counter-strike package of the post-MOU period. The first fireman killed in the exchange was confirmed (Iranshahr airport). On the MOU's formal status: no formal termination instrument was issued. No US executive order or CENTCOM order reinstating the naval blockade was confirmed as of the July 9 evening brief. No SNSC formal MOU-void declaration was issued. The re-closure declaration operative since June 26 remains under the prior IRGC cargo-strike rationale — Iran has not issued a new MOU-void claim in response to the July 8 oil sanctions reimposition or the additional CENTCOM strikes. The critical analytical distinction is between Trump's declaratory 'over' language (rhetorical maximum-pressure posture, consistent with his historical negotiating pattern) and the formal legal-military status of the MOU (no termination instrument). The survival thread: Trump explicitly acknowledged 'Steve and Jared want to keep going — but they have to come back to me.' Witkoff and Kushner publicly confirmed desire to continue negotiations. Trump 'did not rule out talks continuing' per multiple outlets. This dual-track posture — maximum rhetorical pressure plus preserved negotiator channel — is the same pattern that characterized the May 19 'attack called off at Gulf allies' request' episode, the June 2 Iran comms suspension resolution, and multiple prior escalation-and-pull-back sequences in the 132-day arc. The key unknown entering July 9 evening: whether the SNSC formally characterizes the oil sanctions reimposition as a US MOU breach requiring a formal SNSC void declaration — which would be the single most escalatory possible step — or whether the SNSC tacitly allows the re-escalation to remain within the managed-pressure framework. As of this session, no SNSC formal declaration has been confirmed. Kharg Island was not struck. The MOU framework is under maximum declaratory stress but formally intact. WTI at ~$75 on July 9 reflects the re-escalation premium returning after 12 days below the $74 normalization floor ($69 range). This is a war-risk premium price, not a normalization-confidence price — the directional signal is deteriorating, not improving, relative to the deal-day $74 floor established June 19.

items.summary: Five secondary geopolitical threads on July 9 evening. First: Russia fuel crisis Day 9. Omsk refinery — Russia's largest refinery and top domestic gasoline producer — halted operations on July 7 after Ukrainian drone strikes on July 6. Two industry sources confirmed operational halt. This is the crisis's single most consequential infrastructure event: Omsk processes approximately 20 million metric tons of crude annually. Combined with prior strikes, approximately one-quarter to one-third of Russia's national refining capacity is now offline. Daily gasoline shortfall running approximately 20% below domestic demand. 78 of 83 internationally recognized Russian regions reporting fuel access disruptions. IEA 'unprecedented' designation holds. Sales rationed to 20-30 liters per vehicle in affected regions. For Chair Warsh's September SEP deflationary impulse to hold, both Hormuz and Russian refining need to be resolving — neither is resolving on July 9. The FOMC minutes (June 17 meeting) predate the Russia fuel crisis's onset (approximately July 1), meaning the committee's June assessment did not incorporate this new supply disruption. Second: Lebanon fragile hold Day 24. The June 30 Iran-US-Lebanon ceasefire oversight committee — formed to coordinate the end of the 2026 Lebanon war — is nominally active. Hezbollah's 'null and void' declaration on the Rubio framework remains unretracted. IDF incursion tempo remains reduced but no formal recommitment. The July 8-9 CENTCOM-Iran exchange adds uncertainty: if Iran characterizes the strikes as license to direct Hezbollah to resume operations, the Lebanon 'null and void' declaration becomes an operational trigger. No such direction has been confirmed as of this session. Third: Peru Keiko Fujimori is T-6 days from the JNE congressional credentials ceremony (July 15). Inauguration July 28 (T-19). The Andean resource nationalism premium eliminated at JNE certification continues to hold — copper and silver markets are not re-pricing Peru political risk at the current stage. Fourth: Colombia de la Espriella transition Day 7 (T-29 to August 7 inauguration). Israel relations restoration pledged; no transition complications confirmed. Fifth: Venezuela earthquake Day 16 — 1,719+ confirmed dead, 46,600+ missing. Maduro government continues to restrict USAID and FEMA humanitarian access. De la Espriella's Colombia (T-29 to inauguration) will face immediate cross-border humanitarian pressure.

items.summary: The July 9 energy and monetary picture is structurally inverted from the normalization narrative: WTI is above the $74 normalization confidence floor for the first time since Day 12 below the floor — but the directional signal is deteriorating, not improving. Oil sanctions on Iranian crude were reimposed July 7, stripping the MOU's central economic incentive for Iranian participation. WTI rose 4.4% on July 8 to close at $73.52, then gained another 2.2% on July 9 to top $75 per barrel. This price movement is a war-risk premium, not a deal-stability premium: the market is pricing the probability that Kharg Island — through which 90% of Iran's oil exports transit — could be struck, that the CENTCOM blockade could be reinstated, and that the IRGC would respond by fully closing Hormuz at the physical (not merely declaratory) level. For the MOU normalization pathway, WTI above $74 from war risk is the worst possible signal: the commodity market is pricing in supply disruption rather than supply normalization. The Hormuz normalization thesis required WTI to decline below $74 and sustain, signaling market confidence in the compliance trajectory. Instead, WTI has returned above $74 under an escalation premium, meaning Lloyd's war-risk rates are moving higher rather than lower. On the FOMC minutes (released July 8): the 9-9 split on 2026 hikes and Warsh's deliberate withholding of his own dot made Tuesday's minutes the sole on-record committee direction signal. September hike odds settled at 50-55% after release (down from 66%). Warsh's 130-word June 17 policy statement stripped all forward guidance. The next FOMC communication event will need to incorporate both the Russia fuel crisis (which postdates the June 17 meeting) and the July 8-9 Hormuz re-escalation's energy price implications — both are inflationary pressures that complicate the September deflationary-impulse thesis. On the tariff calendar: Section 122 expires July 24 (T-15). The USTR Section 301 public hearing on the proposed 12.5% tariff (46 countries) and 10% tariff (15 countries, including EU, Canada, UK, Mexico) concluded July 7. The post-hearing review period is now active; no announcement of a finalized Section 301 framework has been made as of this session. Importers face a 15-day planning gap between the Section 122 expiry and whatever Section 301 successor takes effect.

items.summary: The July 9 infrastructure session records the most significant fire management progress of the post-July 4 outbreak. The Chelan Hills Fire (Day 5, ~9,735 acres, 50% containment) has achieved the week's pivotal containment milestone — moving from the zero-containment generational-destruction crisis framing of Days 1-3 to majority-containment managed-suppression framing by Day 5. The 50% figure represents containment line geometry established on approximately half the fire's perimeter — in the east-of-Cascades WUI terrain of Douglas County (Orondo to Chelan Falls corridor) where dozer access is available. This is categorically the most significant domestic fire management achievement of the 2026 season to date. At Day 3 (July 6), Chelan Hills stood at zero containment with 100+ structures destroyed and Douglas County Fire Marshal Tyler Caille characterizing it as the most destructive fire in his 30-year career. At Day 5 (July 9), the structural loss is stabilized, personnel are transitioning from initial attack geometry to extended containment operations, and the evacuation zone is unchanged (Level 3 for Orondo, Chelan Falls, Chelan Hills corridor) pending further perimeter consolidation. One confirmed fatality (human remains found in burned vehicle) remains the fire's death toll. Some media estimates placed the fire at 15,000-20,000 acres at peak spread; the official ICS-209 footprint as of this session is ~9,735 acres, reflecting the controlled measurement methodology. The Navarre Coulee Fire (near Lake Chelan, same Douglas/Chelan county geographic zone) has been substantially de-escalated: 300 acres, 80% contained, Level 1 evacuation advisory only, no structures lost. The downgrade from Level 2 to Level 1 and 80% containment effectively removes Navarre Coulee from the active threat roster. Both Highways 97 and 97A are open for travel. The Sourdough Fire (Day 5, North Cascades NP, Whatcom County WA) is the session's primary infrastructure uncertainty. The atmospheric river that provided aerial suppression cover July 5-8 closed its window on July 8 night. The Day 5 ICS-209 — due in the July 9 morning reporting cycle — is the first post-AR-window containment figure and the definitive indicator of whether initial attack geometry was established during the AR window. Any containment percentage would confirm the aerial attack teams used the AR humidity recovery to establish perimeter geometry in the roadless North Cascades wilderness. The SR-20 status (closed indefinitely as of July 8 between Newhalem and Silver Star gate, ~22 miles) and Skagit dam hydropower restoration (Gorge, Diablo, Ross dams; Seattle City Light supply disrupted) are both gated on the Sourdough fire proximity to the Skagit dam complex. Sources indicating SR-20 has reopened (King5, KIRO7 reporting of a North Cascades highway reopening in the context of the current fires) are consistent with meaningful AR-period fire containment progress — but no confirmed official reopening has been independently verified for the July 9 session as of this writing. NIFC Preparedness Level 4 (Day 11, first PL4 since 2021) remains active with 37 large fires nationally. North Cayuse Fire (east of Pendleton, OR) remains active with evacuations. Crawford Oaks Fire (Dallesport WA, Columbia Gorge) is at structure-threat status.

items.summary: Four secondary infrastructure threads on July 9 evening. First: FERC AI pathway intervention deadline closed at COB today. This procedural closure is significant: all parties who filed notices of intervention are now locked into the six ISO/RTO show cause proceedings on large-load integration reform. Non-filers are excluded from the formal docket. The stakeholder map — utility companies, data center developers, consumer advocates, state commissions, independent power producers — is now complete. The 30-day informational report deadline (July 18, T-9) is the next hard deadline: each of the six grid operators must explain how they plan to ensure sufficient generation for existing customers plus new large loads. The 60-day show cause/tariff response (August 17, T-39) is when operators must justify or revise large-load tariff frameworks. For PNW data center corridors (Quincy WA, The Dalles OR, Eastern Oregon — BPA/WECC jurisdiction, outside the six ISO/RTO direct scope), the proceedings set de facto national standards. BPA's role as the Pacific Northwest's primary federal power marketer — and the data center build-out's primary power source — means the July 18 and August 17 deadlines matter structurally for PNW AI infrastructure capacity planning. Second: NSF Newport, Oregon ocean observatory remains dark at Day 11. The most recent major weather event in the monitoring gap — the July 5-8 atmospheric river — produced flood watches for SW Washington and NW Oregon, which NWS Portland issued without the Newport coastal anchor. The degraded coastal calibration has now been operationally confirmed twice (AR event) during the monitoring gap period. items.summary: The July 9 PNW fire session represents the week's inflection point — from the generational-crisis framing of Days 1-3 to a managed-containment framing by Day 5, anchored by the Chelan Hills Fire's 50% containment milestone. The Chelan Hills Fire's arc over five days encapsulates the 2026 PNW fire season's structural character: fourth-consecutive drought year, record-low snowpack, NIFC PL4 resource scarcity, and east-of-Cascades WUI terrain with high structural density combine to produce extreme initial fire behavior (100+ structures lost, 0% containment at Day 3) that transitions to meaningful containment only once sustained aerial and dozer resources are deployed at scale. At 50% containment with the ~9,735-acre official footprint, the Chelan Hills Fire is entering the extended-suppression phase. Line geometry is established on the dominant perimeter segments. Personnel can shift from initial attack resource prioritization to mop-up and perimeter consolidation on the contained sections. The one confirmed fatality (human remains in burned vehicle) is the fire's total death toll. Level 3 evacuations remain active for the Orondo-Chelan Falls corridor — the final operational decision for downgrade will follow perimeter consolidation and structural condition assessment in the evacuation zone. Highways 97 and 97A are open, facilitating supply and personnel movement. Navarre Coulee (300 acres, 80% contained, Level 1) is functionally resolved. The Sourdough Fire's July 9 status hinges on the Day 5 ICS-209 that should be available in the morning reporting cycle. The atmospheric river suppression window closed July 8 night — the aerial-only attack teams had July 5-8 to establish any perimeter geometry in the roadless North Cascades wilderness of Sourdough Ridge/Diablo Lake (Whatcom County). If the Day 5 ICS-209 shows any containment percentage, it confirms the AR window was productively used and initial attack geometry is established. This would enable the progression toward SR-20 reopening and Skagit dam power restoration — significant quality-of-life and energy-grid milestones for Whatcom County and Seattle City Light. Multiple local outlet reports are consistent with SR-20 having been reopened during or shortly after the AR window — suggesting the Sourdough fire's perimeter proximity to the SR-20 corridor reduced sufficiently for road crews to assess reopening. If confirmed, SR-20 reopening and Skagit dam power restoration signal the Sourdough transitioning toward extended attack at a stable perimeter, not a rapidly expanding emergency. BPA continues managing the grid transition from heat-wave peak demand reduction to summer baseline, with Skagit hydropower supply partial reduction still active pending fire proximity clearance. NIFC PL4 Day 11 maintains the national resource constraint context — Chelan Hills, Sourdough, North Cayuse OR, and Crawford Oaks WA are simultaneously competing for aerial tanker and helicopter assets in a PL4 nationally-constrained environment.
